I will keep my main land in the wheat-maize rotation because that is the most stable way for me to use my 13.1 mu, my well water, and the labor my family can still organize even though some people work off-farm. I will put 9.0 mu into winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land, and I will keep 4.1 mu in cotton. I do not want to spread myself too thin with too many different arrangements. I have farmed a long time, so I will stay with the crops and field practices I trust most, but I will use better seed where it gives me steadier yield.

For wheat, I will use improved seed, give enough nitrogen for strong early growth and grain filling, and irrigate twice because wheat here responds well when water is available. I will use rotary tillage because it fits my usual wheat field preparation and is manageable. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because I want stronger yield on the summer crop, and I will keep fertilizer fairly strong since maize follows wheat and needs to grow fast. I will use no-tillage for maize after wheat to save time and labor at the tight turnover between crops. For cotton, I will keep a smaller area because it needs more management and more pesticide sprays, but I still want it as a cash crop. I will fertilize cotton more evenly, include more potassium, irrigate when needed from the well, and expect lower yield per mu than grain but better cash return if managed carefully.
